sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Methods are like recipes in programming - they let you reuse code and keep things organized! Here's what we'll cover:

• What methods are and why they're useful
• How to create and call your own methods
• The parts that make up a method (name, parameters, return type)
• How methods help you write cleaner code

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine you're baking cookies. Instead of writing the same instructions every time you want cookies, you create a recipe card (method) that you can use again and again.

Methods work the same way in programming! They let you:

• **Package code** into reusable blocks
• **Avoid repetition** - write once, use many times
• **Organize your program** into logical pieces

Here's a simple method that says hello:
```java
void sayHello() {
    System.out.println("Hello!");
}
```

• `void` means it doesn't return anything
• `sayHello` is the method name
• The curly braces `{}` contain the code to run

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: A method is a named block of code that performs a specific task and can be reused
Methods promote code reuse, organization, and stepwise refinement
A method header specifies the return type, method name, and parameter list
The method body contains the statements that execute when the method is called
Methods reduce code duplication and make programs easier to maintain

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Methods help you organize and reuse code. Every method has a name, parameters (optional), and a body. Call methods by using their name followed by parentheses. Practice creating simple methods before moving to more complex ones.
